name: NIST 6061-T6 Aluminum Fatigue Life (Birnbaum & Saunders 1958)
license_name: NIST Public Domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. § 105)
failure_mode: Fatigue rupture (all specimens tested to complete failure)
censoring_semantics: All 101 specimens are complete failure observations. No censoring, no runouts, no suspensions. Every data point is a failure time (thousands of cycles until rupture).
inclusion_rule: All 101 observations are included. Single stress level, single material batch, single failure mode, complete observations only.
original_reference: Birnbaum, Z. W. and Saunders, S. C. (1958), 'A Statistical Model for Life-Length of Materials', Journal of the American Statistical Association, 53(281), pp. 151-160.
homogeneity_notes: All specimens are from the same material (6061-T6 aluminum alloy sheeting), tested under identical conditions (periodic loading, max stress 21,000 psi), with a single failure mode (fatigue rupture). No stratification by stress level, temperature, or batch is needed.
data_extraction_method: Values extracted from NIST webpage <pre> block at eda4291.htm, cross-verified against BIRNSAUN.DAT raw file (SHA256 above). Sorted order in lifetimes.csv matches NIST page layout (row-major, 6 columns × 16 rows + 5 in last row = 101 values).
weibull_suitability: This dataset has been extensively used as a Weibull distribution case study in the NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook itself (§1.4.2.9). The handbook compares Weibull, lognormal, and Birnbaum-Saunders distributions. Three-parameter Weibull is a canonical model for this data in the reliability engineering literature.
